submission.justification:
Radiator-R2 at 3 cm thickness is recommended as it achieves the best pion/kaon separation performance of 4.6σ at 10 GeV/c, which is 16.5% better than R1's optimal performance (3.949σ at 2 cm) and 58.6% better than R3's optimal performance (2.849σ at 2 cm). 

While R2 is porous and untreated (presenting a stability risk factor of 1 compared to 0 for R1 and R3), the task documents indicate that dry nitrogen protection is available to mitigate degradation risks. This environmental control measure addresses the lifetime performance constraint, allowing R2 to maintain its superior separation capability throughout the experiment's lifetime.

The simulation data clearly shows R2 provides the best separation across the thickness range, with its optimal performance at 3 cm (within the 1-6 cm constraint). This configuration achieves the stated goal of "best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c" while satisfying all constraints when operated with appropriate environmental protection.
